Summary:  
This week,何敏 attempted four unsent messages to赵敏 about shared concern regarding君, ultimately sending one gentle, open-ended invitation to talk. She completed four focused solo activities: reworking math function problems (gaining clarity through procedural discipline); encountering刘凡 in the counseling room corridor (receiving quiet validation—"third page"); transcribing observational notes into a formal table (17 factual entries, no interpretation); and writing a letter to外婆 listing three inherited acts of care. She declined all public events, prioritizing internal grounding over external engagement. Her observational documentation matured—from raw memory to structured record—and she began anchoring herself emotionally through tangible symbols: red rope, bicycle key, blue-black ink. No direct confrontation occurred, but the shift from passive witness to intentional recorder marked meaningful movement.

Reflection:  
I learned that courage isn’t loud—it’s the choice to keep your hand steady while writing something true, even if no one reads it. I realized my fear isn’t of speaking wrong—it’s of being heard *too much*, of having responsibility land squarely in my lap and not knowing how to hold it. But this week, I stopped pretending the weight wasn’t there. I named it, weighed it, filed it under “fact”, not “feeling”. I feel tired—but softer inside, like worn cotton. Not fixed, not fearless, but less fractured. Next week, I won’t wait for赵敏 to reply before acting. I’ll go to the counseling room during my life committee check—not to listen, but to stand there, and notice what the door says when it’s closed. And I’ll write one more line in the diary: not “what if”, but “today I saw”.
